answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy works through stake-weighted identity on a shared ledger: each agent must post ferrous-token collateral that stays locked before it can vote or earn, and the ledger caps how many identities one funding source may back. Forging a thousand puppet agents then means posting a thousand real stakes, so a fake knoll of accounts costs the attacker the full locked sum rather than a free script. A verified haven where nodes vouch for shared work raises the price further, since puppets must also outbid honest operators and forfeit collateral after each ban.
